text: You're at the store, just a few items. Now, the familiar challenge: which checkout line do you pick? You survey the options, hoping for the fastest path.
You make your choice, step in, and almost immediately, the lane next to you surges forward. Your lane, of course, slows to a crawl.
You glance around, convinced you picked the one slow queue. It feels like a personal curse, a cosmic joke just for you, every single time.
But here’s the invisible system: for every lane you are in, there are several you are NOT. And you only *switch* when yours is slow.
You remember the times you were stuck, but rarely the times you zipped through. This memory bias makes every slow moment feel like the rule.
Next time you’re stuck, remember: you’re just experiencing the average. The other lanes aren’t always faster; you just notice them more when they are.
